footnotes.text: The whole trick. Water at i is min(tallest left, tallest right) − height[i]. We don't know both maxima for every column - but we only need the smaller one, and whichever side has the smaller max is already decided.

steps.t: Two pointers start at the outer walls: l = 0, r = 11.
Tallest wall seen from the left: 0. From the right: 1.
max_l = 0 < max_r = 1, so the LEFT side is the bottleneck. Somewhere on the right there is a wall at least 1 tall, so the water just right of l is decided by max_l alone.
Move l to 1 (height 2). max_l is now 2.
Column 1 holds max_l − height[1] = 2 − 2 = 0. Total: 0.
